title: Receptor-level bypass
detail: MET amplification; activating NRAS/BRAF/MAP2K1/RET; ALK/RET/BRAF/RAF1/FGFR3 fusions. MET keeps RAS GTP-loaded through SOS1 rather than bypassing it

title: Downstream MAPK nodes
detail: BRAF, MAP2K1, NRAS, RAF1 reactivate ERK without passing through RAS; rarely alone - 10 alterations across 4 genes in one patient's serial cfDNA

title: Parallel chains
detail: PI3K-AKT-mTOR and YAP1/TAZ; YAP1/TAZ drives resistance with no ERK rebound. The weight of PI3K-AKT is disputed and the two studies used different tissues

title: Cell state
detail: A classical epithelial state confers acute resistance with no new mutation; transcriptional reprogramming was found in all eight resistant biopsies, including those with genetic hits

title: Lineage exit
detail: Adeno-to-squamous transition (LKB1-deficient), Paneth-like state under dual KRAS/EGFR blockade, quiescent AT1-like state. The squamous signature is already visible before treatment

title: Proteostasis
detail: How much protein is left: KRAS inhibition suppresses the heat-shock response and IRE1a; resistant tumours reactivate IRE1a. Named convergence point of several mechanisms

title: Polarity and cytoskeleton
detail: Where the protein goes: the YAP-MRAS axis

title: Signalling condensates
detail: How it is organised locally: the disordered ARAF N terminus self-assembles into membrane-tethered ARAF-RAS condensates that concentrate active RAS and defeat NF1

title: Metabolic reprogramming
detail: Two separate things: whether the membrane still holds the protein (mevalonate pathway; statin-reversible) and how the cell makes energy (OXPHOS-dependent state with ZBTB11 as its hub)
